meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: With a smile he always softens up.

meanings.note: Plural los abuelos also means 'grandparents'.

examples.trans: The grandfather is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abuelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandfathers from the door.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.trans: It is a yellow piece.

examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Tall, light home-baked cake popular for breakfast or afternoon merienda in Spain.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bizcochos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sponge cakes from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Coger cariño a = to grow fond of; also a warm term of endearment in Spain.

examples.text: El cariño es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The affection is very important here.

meanings.note: Wicker kitchen or market basket.

examples.trans: The basket is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cestas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the baskets from the door.

meanings.note: Fruncir el ceño means 'to frown'.

examples.trans: The brow is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ceños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brows from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: consigo, consiguió).

examples.text: Siempre consigue mesa junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: She always gets a table by the window.

examples.text: Por fin conseguimos abrir el cofre.
examples.trans: We finally managed to open the chest.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Corto el pan en rebanadas finas.

examples.text: La panadera cortó cuatro trozos de bizcocho.
examples.trans: The baker cut four pieces of sponge cake.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a crispy piece.
Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.

meanings.note: Por nuestra culpa = because of us; no es culpa suya = it is not your fault.

examples.trans: The fault is here.

examples.text: Vemos las culpas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the faults from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.trans: What is your name?
How do I find the hardware shop?

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (salir directo = walk straight out).

examples.trans: It is a direct piece.

examples.text: Sí, Rocío. Aunque dé media vuelta y salga directo por la puerta.
examples.trans: Yes, Rocio. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.

meanings.note: Hacerse el duro = to act tough.

examples.trans: It is a hard piece.
acted tough

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?
Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

meanings.note: Fallar una nota = to miss a musical note.

examples.trans: That lock almost never fails.

examples.text: Falló una sola nota en toda la pieza.
examples.trans: He missed only a single note in the whole piece.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.en: to wrinkle; to furrow (fruncir el ceño = to frown)

examples.text: Siempre frunces el ceño cuando lees.
examples.trans: You always wrinkle your brow when reading.

examples.text: Frunció el ceño al mirar la cuenta.
examples.trans: He frowned when looking at the bill.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la pared, las paredes.

examples.text: Vemos las paredes desde la puerta.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Pelearse por algo = to squabble over something.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Vemos los pianos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pianos from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

examples.trans: It is a still piece.

examples.text: Quietos los dos. ¿Oyen ese motor parando junto al bordillo?
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Esta mañana recibí una carta certificada.
examples.trans: This morning I received a registered letter.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: recuerdo).

examples.trans: I remember that afternoon perfectly.
Do you remember where we put the blueprint?

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

meanings.note: Conjugates like reír (sonrío, sonrió); imperative plural: ¡sonreíd!.

examples.text: La panadera siempre sonríe al abrir el horno.

examples.text: Al probar el bizcocho, sonrió enseguida.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.

meanings.note: After a verb, invariable tanto means 'so much' (¿por qué mira tanto?).

examples.trans: How do you remember that after so many years?
Thank you for having so much patience.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Pleasantly warm (not scalding hot).

examples.text: Toque el radiador: arriba está templado, pero abajo se está enfriando.
examples.trans: Touch the radiator: the top is lukewarm, yet the bottom is getting cold.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.
He smiled again right away.

vuelta.gloss: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)

meanings.en: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)
meanings.note: Dar una vuelta = take a stroll / make one turn.

examples.trans: The turn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vueltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the turns from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
